articles.title: South Africa v Australia: third men’s one-day international – live
articles.summary: Updates from the ODI match at NWC Oval. Start time in Potchefstroom is 1.30pm local/9.30pm AEST. Any thoughts? Get in touch with an email. 2nd over: Australia 10-0 (Marsh 5, Head 5) And the quiet times lasted one over! First Head, then Marsh, play pull shots from Williams for four.
body: 9th over: South Africa 49-2 (Rickelton 27, Breetzke 6) Pat Cummins replaces Starc to bowl for the first time on this South African tour. His third ball is a fraction too short and Rickelton swivels on a pull shot and deposits him onto the grass embankment for six either side of singles for both batters.

8th over: South Africa 41-2 (Rickelton 20, Breetzke 5) Bartlett has been so good. He’s working out his lengths and curating them for each batter in real time. When he over-pitches to Rickelton he’s driven down the ground for four. But when he pulls it back a touch he’s beating the lefty’s outside edge with some lovely movement off the surface. Two more are added to the score with a thickish edge off Rickelton’s bat to deep third and a drop and run from Breetzke.
7th over: South Africa 35-2 (Rickelton 15, Breetzke 4) After all the excitement from the last over, Starc chills things out with some top of off stuff. Just the one single for Rickelton off that set.

articles.title: 'Business as usual' for Man City Women despite Premier League guilty verdicts
articles.summary: Manchester City manager Andree Jeglertz said it was "business as usual" for the women's team despite the Premier League charges against the club.
body: Manchester City manager Andree Jeglertz did not comment on whether he had received assurances that the women's team would not be impacted after the club was found guilty of Premier League financial breaches.
Jeglertz, who joined City last summer, said it was "business as usual" and when asked about how the women's team could be affected, added: "I don't want to comment more around that."
There were seven questions in total posed to Jeglertz relating to the charges before Manchester City's press officer requested the media moved away from it.
The club has been found guilty of all charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

articles.title: ‘We don’t need boos’: Astros players frustrated as own fans turn on them in playoffs
articles.summary: Houston announce crowd of 34,011 for playoff opener. Players criticize boos during 6-3 defeat by White Sox. Astros are first division winner with.500 or worse mark. The crowd at Daikin Park was surprisingly sparse as the Houston Astros – baseball’s first division winner with a.500 or worse record …
body: Large swaths of seats, especially in the upper deck, sat empty while right-hander AJ Blumbaugh delivered the game’s first pitch at 4.10pm. The bottom two levels were much fuller than the upper deck, but many seats in the lower two decks were also empty.
The announced attendance was 34,011, in a park with a capacity of 40,963.

All those empty seats are a rare sight in a stadium that is normally packed for the postseason. And some of the fans that did show up weren’t too happy with the performance of the home team with boos raining down on the Astros in the first and second innings as they fell behind 3-0.

“It’s extremely frustrating as a home player,” first baseman Christian Walker told the Athletic. “We’re here, playing at home; we need cheers. We need energy. We don’t need boos. What purpose does that serve in that moment? Whatever fans are feeling, we’re feeling it tenfold. We’re the ones out there. We’re the ones in the fight. We worked our butts off this whole season to put ourselves in this spot, and for guys to get booed, it’s frustrating.”

articles.summary: Keeper pulled out of both Nations League games with Israel. Hallgrímsson confident Sunday’s second match will go ahead. body: Ireland are one of Europe’s most outspoken critics of Israel’s war in Gaza, ⁠and protests calling for the team to boycott the fixture prompted Bazunu to pull out of both games between the two countries.

Last Sunday’s match, which Ireland won 3-0, went ahead after a majority of their squad ⁠voted to play on the eve of the away fixture in Hungary. Media reports indicated a fractured squad after the meeting and ​vote, and that Bazunu had been insulted by teammates ‌over his decision.

The keeper is ‌available for Thursday’s home game with Austria, but will not take part in Sunday’s rematch with Israel, which the Football Association ‌of Ireland (FAI) has moved to Serbia behind closed doors.

“Gavin is a great lad, I’ve always had a good relationship with him and it’s probably tougher for him than the other players, but they have really welcomed him,” Hallgrímsson told a press conference on Wednesday.

articles.title: English players urged to reconsider Afghan T20 tournament
articles.summary: English cricketers aiming to play in a men's T20 franchise tournament organised by the Afghanistan Cricket Board have been urged to think about their "daughters, sisters or mothers".
body: The inaugural edition of the Afghanistan Premier League (APL) will be staged in the United Arab Emirates later this year.

England players Ollie Pope and Luke Wood have both registered for the tournament draft, held in October, along with fellow Englishmen Moeen Ali, Reece Topley, James Vince, Tom Kohler-Cadmore and Laurie Evans.
Their involvement comes despite the England and Wales Cricket Board's (ECB) refusal to schedule bilateral men's cricket against Afghanistan because of the Taliban's treatment of women and girls.
BBC Sport understands the ECB's policy does not extend to franchise tournaments, meaning players can decide for themselves whether to participate.

articles.summary: Fifteen-year-old Indian cricket sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has been named on a prestigious list identifying the world's most influential rising stars.
body: The 2026 Time100 Next list features 100 emerging talents who Time Magazine foresees as influencing their respective fields, including sport, entertainment, politics and business.
Sooryavanshi is the youngest person to be listed and is among seven athletes named.

Athletes joining Sooryavanshi include American football quarterback Arch Manning, NBA star Tyrese Maxey, footballers Naomi Girma and Folarin Balogun, tennis player Alexandra Eala and basketball player Olivia Miles.

articles.title: What if Man City's Premier League titles and trophies are stripped?
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher has called for Manchester City to be stripped of their titles after the club was found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules – so what would change?
body: An independent commission found City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, during which the club won three Premier League titles, one FA Cup, three League Cups and one Community Shield.

Sanctions will be addressed in a further hearing with the independent commission and Man City, who continue to deny the breaches, have confirmed they will appeal against the ruling and have until Friday, October 2 to do so.
Possible sanctions include points deductions, fines, transfer bans and expulsion from the Premier League - but what if City are stripped of their titles and trophies?

They pipped Manchester United on the final day of the season in 2012 through Sergio Aguero's famous winner, then they won the league by two points over Liverpool in 2014 before setting a new record in 2018 by amassing 100 points to deny United again.

articles.title: Arizona State places men's hockey coach Greg Powers on administrative leave
articles.summary: Zac BonDurant via Getty Images. Arizona State men’s hockey head coach Greg Powers has been placed on paid administrative leave in the wake of a workout that left sophomore Matthew Mayich on life support and in a coma in August.
body: "The concerns raised by student-athletes deserve to be heard and thoroughly reviewed,” said the National Collegiate Hockey Conference, where the Sun Devils are a member, in a statement. “We will not prejudge the findings of that review. Hockey matters deeply to our conference, but the well-being of our student-athletes matters more."

The decision comes days after players and Mayich’s parents called for Powers to be placed on leave. Seven Sun Devils players wrote a 26-page letter to Arizona State president Michael Crow on Monday, which was obtained by The Athletic. They wrote the letter anonymously through an attorney, as they said they fear retaliation from Powers.

The players disputed several findings from the university's initial review of the Aug. 20 workout that resulted in Mayich's collapse, including that he did not receive water and was provided inadequate medical care after collapsing.

The Sun Devils open their season on Friday and assistant Mike Corbett will assume coaching duties while Powers is away from the team. An interim head coach will reportedly be named soon, according to the Grand Forks Herald’s Brad Elliott Schlossman.

articles.summary: Ask a Formula 1 driver or fan anytime over the last nine years what track they would most like to see return to the sport's calendar, and there was a good chance that Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit would get mentioned.
body: So those who have been hoping that Sepang would one day return get their wish this weekend as, for the first time since 2017, Formula 1 cars will race on the fast, flowing 3.44-mile track on the outskirts of Kuala Lumpur.
We take a look at how that has unexpectedly come about and what to expect from the race weekend...
The first thing to explain is how Malaysia has ended up as the host of Bahrain's Grand Prix.

The Bahrain Grand Prix at the Gulf country's own Sakhir track had been scheduled to take place on April 12 but the war in the Middle East saw both their race and Saudi Arabia's, which was scheduled for the week after, called off.

articles.title: Who wins the Arc? Jamie Lynch's big-race runner guide
articles.summary: Our Senior Form Analyst looks ahead to Europe's most prestigious contest, live on Sky Sports Racing on Sunday, and reveals his big-race fancy.
body: Daryz bids to defend his Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe crown at Parislongchamp on Sunday and out Senior Form Analyst Jamie Lynch has provided a runner-by-runner guide to the coveted Group One contest.

This is everything a Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe should be, first and foremost a clash of nations and generations, and not just a defining race but a deciding race, to decide the best around, while a returning champion always adds an extra layer of motivation and invigoration.

Roger Varian's fourth runner in an Arc, after Kingston Hill's fourth in 2014 and Postponed's fifth (as favourite) in 2016, and Defoe was done by stall 18 in 2018. Saddadd isn't rated nor decorated like any of those, but he's still pushing upwards, a master of marginal gains, taking him from a London Gold Cup to a German Group One, and the Grosser Preis von Baden has had a happy habit of readying Arc winners, like Marienbard, Danedream and Torquator Tasso. That was only his first go at the trip, yet he was fastest at stages of both the Tattersalls Gold Cup and the Coral-Eclipse, Group Ones at a mile and a quarter, and the systematic skin-shedding qualifies him as a lively longshot.
